newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, Belarus parliament heads urge compromise.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Belarus parliament heads urge compromise.

text.p: Parliamentary leaders from Russia and Belarus, meeting on Russian soil, appealed on Wednesday for a compromise to be found to end the political dispute in Belarus, Interfax news agency reported.

It said the parliamentary chiefs, meeting in the Russian city of Smolensk, would inform President Alexander Lukashenko and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin about their talks but did not make clear if they had made any breakthrough.
Gennady Seleznyov and Yegor Stroyev, the leaders of Russia's two houses of parliament, met Belarus parliament chairman Semyon Sharetsky in Smolensk to try to defuse the crisis.
Lukashenko, whose plans for a referendum on increasing his powers are opposed by the Belarus parliament, did not attend.

"We appealed for the need to search for compromise decisions between the two branches of power in Belarus, for the need of cerefully considered and tolerant relations between the two sides in the conflict," Interfax quoted Stroyev as saying.
The agency did not carry any statements by members of the Belarus delegation.
